patch_description: This replaces path-selection rewards with a cut-capacity model. For each two- and three-node set, it estimates the traffic that must cross its outgoing and incoming boundaries. Selecting links internal to the set reduces boundary capacity, so a second-order expansion of a convex congestion proxy produces linear and pairwise QUBO costs. The pairwise terms are sparse and arise from shared cuts, rather than from chosen two-hop routes. Direct-demand rewards remain as a tie-breaker when cut loads are similar.
